description: Hospital's group-purchasing-organization (non-340B) acquisition cost for one levonorgestrel-releasing IUD device
source: Physicians' Alliance of America, 'Liletta Pricing Update' (secondary-source summary; direct fetch of the underlying MDedge article was truncated and did NOT independently confirm these figures -- re-fetch and verify before treating this as a settled value)
notes: Base case is the midpoint of a $537 (with volume discount) to $600 (without) range reported by a physician-group pricing bulletin, not yet independently verified against a primary GPO contract or invoice. This is the number that should anchor the base case IF the hospital doing the bariatric surgery is NOT 340B-eligible.

description: Hospital's 340B-program acquisition cost for one Liletta levonorgestrel IUD, for a 340B-eligible (safety-net/disproportionate-share) hospital
source: AAFCPAs, 'LILETTA IUD May Offer Cost Savings to 340B Covered Entities' (2016-09-12), citing a Medicines360 pricing announcement
notes: STALE PRICE WARNING: this $50 figure is from a 2016 announcement stating the price 'would never increase'; an unverified secondary source suggests it was later raised to $100. Needs direct re-verification against Medicines360's current price list before use. Relevant because the hospital in this model's real MRF extract (Denver Health) is a safety-net/DSH hospital and is plausibly, but not confirmedly, 340B-eligible.

description: Denver Health's own published self-pay/discounted-cash price for HCPCS J7297 (levonorgestrel IUD, 52mg, 8yr), from its CMS-mandated price-transparency machine-readable file
source: Denver Health and Hospital Authority standard-charges MRF, downloaded directly 2026-09-10 from https://sthpiprd.blob.core.windows.net/machine-readable-files/7840/841343242_denver-health-and-hospital-authority_standardcharges.csv (file dated 2026-04-30); gross charge $2,393.32, discounted-cash $837.67, inpatient negotiated-equivalent $820.91
notes: Directly verified, single-institution primary source -- not a national estimate. Provided as a cross-check ceiling, NOT the base-case acquisition cost: chargemaster/cash prices include hospital margin above true acquisition cost, which is exactly why iud_device_acquisition_cost_gpo and _340b (far lower) are used for the actual cost-minimization base case.

description: Physician professional fee for IUD insertion (CPT 58300)
source: Base value: Denver Health MRF, CPT 58300, discounted-cash price, downloaded 2026-09-10 (same file as above; gross charge $331.65). Low/high bound: aggregator-reported commercial-payer range ($75-$125), not independently verified against a second primary source.
notes: Only applies to the standalone arm outright. Whether the combined arm also incurs this fee depends on combined_requires_separate_professional_fee below.

description: Evaluation-and-management office-visit cost for a standalone IUD-insertion visit (established patient, CPT 99213)
source: Reused directly from the sibling emb_colonoscopy project's verified extraction: CMS Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service, 2024 (CPT 99213, filtered to Rndrng_Prvdr_Type = 'Obstetrics & Gynecology', live API query 2026-08-28); 12,739 provider-service rows, 686,012 observed services
notes: Not re-pulled fresh for this project -- reused because the underlying claim (real-world OB/GYN E/M visit cost) transfers directly. Low/high are the real p25/p75 from that same claims data.

description: Incremental operating-room minutes for IUD insertion performed at the time of bariatric surgery
source: General (non-bariatric-specific) IUD-under-anesthesia literature: Children's Hospital Colorado / CU Anschutz adolescent-gynecology 'IUD Placement Under Anesthesia' patient-care protocol, stating the insertion itself takes 5-15 minutes.
notes: No published study of IUD insertion added-time specifically during bariatric surgery was found despite multiple targeted literature searches (2026-09-10). This is a general-population proxy, exactly analogous to how the sibling Lynch-syndrome model used non-Lynch-specific literature for its office-EMB failure-rate parameter. Revisit if a bariatric-specific timed study is ever published.

source: Childers CP, Maggard-Gibbons M. Understanding Costs of Care in the Operating Room. JAMA Surg. (reused from the sibling emb_colonoscopy project)
notes: Reused as-is; NOT yet inflation-adjusted to a current reference year in this scaffold (no R/inflation.R wired up yet -- add before reporting any dollar total). The sibling project's 2026-adjusted equivalent was ~$28.73/minute. Low/high = mean +/-1 SD.

description: Anesthesia cost per minute in an operating-room setting
source: Childers CP, Maggard-Gibbons M. Understanding Costs of Care in the Operating Room. JAMA Surg. (reused from the sibling emb_colonoscopy project)
notes: Same inflation-adjustment caveat as direct_room_cost_per_minute above.

description: Scenario toggle: is IUD insertion at time of bariatric surgery billed as a separate professional fee (e.g. a different proceduralist, modifier -59/XU), or bundled/not separately billable because it is a minor procedure added to an already-open case?
source: Model-owner structural assumption, not yet confirmed against a specific payer's bundling policy or a real claim. Default FALSE (bundled/no separate fee) is the more conservative assumption for the combined arm's cost advantage, since it means the combined arm's professional-fee savings are as large as possible.
notes: Toggle to TRUE to test the scenario where the combined arm still incurs iud_insertion_professional_fee separately.

description: Medicare (CMS) negotiated-equivalent inpatient rate for MS-DRG 621, 'O.R. Procedures for Obesity without CC/MCC' -- the host procedure, for context only
source: Denver Health and Hospital Authority standard-charges MRF, downloaded 2026-09-10 (same file as above), payer_name = CMS, plan_name = Medicare
notes: NOT used in the incremental-cost calculation -- the bariatric surgery itself is common to both strategies and cancels out under the incremental-cost principle, exactly as the base colonoscopy cost cancels out in the sibling Lynch-syndrome model. Provided only so a reader can see the host procedure's scale relative to the IUD costs above.
